[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Forms of Address[/color][/head]
How you speak to someone says a lot about who you are and where you stand. Each faction in Taypan has its own culture, and a form of address can signal respect, rivalry, or ignorance. Mistakes happen; if you are new, stay neutral and polite until someone explains the local custom.
This page is a quick guide. For the ranks and roles behind these titles, see the [textlink="Faction Glossary" link="Glossary"].
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Safe defaults[/color][/head]
- With a stranger, use their name or visible job title until you know their faction and preferred form of address. - Ask how someone prefers to be addressed when rank is unclear. Correcting yourself is better roleplay than pretending you knew. - Deliberately misusing a title can create in-character tension, but it should be a character choice rather than an out-of-character trap for a new player.
[head=3][color=#684871]Divine Sol Mandate (DSM)[/color][/head]
The Mandate's charters and estates are built on rank, privilege, duty, and precedent. Address those above you [bold]formally[/bold], because failing to do so is an insult, and before a noble it may even be a crime.
- A knight, such as a Knight Banneret or Knight Templar, is addressed as [color=#684871][bold]Ser[/bold][/color], as in "Yes, Ser" or "As you command, Ser." - Officers and commanders are called [color=#684871][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#684871][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color]. - Nobles and high lords are called [color=#684871][bold]My Lord[/bold][/color] or [color=#684871][bold]My Lady[/bold][/color], or addressed by an office such as Count or Lord Admiral. - Common soldiers, such as a Man-at-Arms or Freeholder, address each other by name or rank, but they always defer upward.
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]New Crescent Workers' League (NCWL)[/color][/head]
The League is the provisional revolutionary front backed by the Workers' Union. It rejects hereditary titles and treats everyone as a comrade in the struggle, while retaining military and administrative offices.
- Everyone is a [color=#bf4d00][bold]Comrade[/bold][/color], as in "Comrade Kapitan" or "well done, comrade." - Civilians and workers may also be called [color=#bf4d00][bold]Citizen[/bold][/color]. - Officers are addressed by their post rather than any lordship, such as MVD Officer, Unionkapitan, or Flagman. - League members normally avoid noble honorifics such as "My Lord." Using one can sound Imperial, submissive, or mocking; "Comrade" plus a post is the safest choice.
[head=3][color=#535961]Shinohara Heavy Industries (SHI)[/color][/head]
Shinohara is a Japanese megacorporation, and its people speak with polished corporate manners. Rank in the company is rank in the room, so be professional and respectful upward.
- Superiors are addressed by their title, such as Sector Manager or Assistant Manager, and a respectful [color=#535961][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#535961][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color] is always safe. - Colleagues may add the honorific [color=#535961][bold]-san[/bold][/color] to a name as a sign of respect. - Rudeness toward a superior is treated as a [color=#d9776c]performance issue[/color], because in Shinohara disloyalty is a threat to the company itself.
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]Taypani Free Companies Federation (TFCF)[/color][/head]
The Federation contains four companies with different internal cultures. Address is usually practical and contractual rather than noble; use a person's company office when it matters.
- The joint leader is the [color=#ff7f7f][bold]Administrator[/bold][/color]. Company leaders remain the proper authority for internal business. - Crewmates are addressed by name, by nickname, or with a blunt "hey." - Gorlex crews favor direct ranks, Interdyne and Cyberdawn use professional titles, and SAW crews tend toward workplace language. A contract matters more than inherited status.
[head=3][color=#4f8b63]TAP, Gliess Santo, and independents[/color][/head]
- Pact crews value family, oath, and practical office. Use a person's role or family name until invited to speak more casually. - On Gliess Santo, station office matters more than an outside title. Dockhands report to the Dockmaster; Militiamen (the Sheriff's deputies) report through the Sheriff and enforce the King's Articles. - Spacers, contractors, pilots, and other independents usually use names, callsigns, or job titles. Their current contract determines who can give them orders.
